title: My Agentic Solution for Investment Works
author: Downtown_Extension_6
selftext:
I built ProspectAI few months ago, just to learn how to implement multi-agentic solutions that resolve a complex workflow usually done by humans. This tool mimics how an investment firm works: a market analyst finds the stocks with better opinions in Reddit, then a parallel flow starts a fundamental and technical analysts, which output is used by draft strategist to create first portfolio. Then a critic agent challenges the strategist to improve the final result.

As I was learning thru iterations, I made this system better and more effective. Up to this point, I am using it as a basis for my own portfolio investments, and I had good results that outpaced my investment in tokens. 

This is not a post for promotion, it is just to explain my experience by using this new technology. I am really surprised to see that across 99 long-buys recommended stocks, 55% are green and the average return is 3.1%, in a window range of less than 3 months. This is without “selling” the bad ones when the stop loss limit is reached, in such case the return would be double-digit.

I charge nothing for using my tool, this is just an individual project I did to complement my professional work, but I encourage you to use it, experiment it and provide any feedback.

S&P was 6575 3 months ago

replies.author: Downtown_Extension_6
replies.body:
Your comparison isn’t apples-to-apples. The picks weren’t all opened 3 months ago. The oldest is Apr 23, but most were opened across mid-May. So measuring them against the S&P from a single fixed date penalizes the recent ones. 

Done right, each signal is compared to the index **over its own holding window**, then averaged.

When you do that: over these exact windows return vs SPY is roughly **+6pp vs SPY**, not −11pp.

Also, these are open paper positions marked-to-market, no stop-losses applied yet.  Cutting the losers at their stops would lift the return to more than 20% across the portfolio, 

If you want to check the math, visit stats link and performance table. https://reports.prospect-ai.moisesprat.dev/stats#performance

replies.author: qqAzo
replies.body:
Done right you look at what return you’d have over the investment period. Not the hold period vs yours. You have x trading days - if you decide to only hold something half the time that’s your strategy’s opportunity cost.

Yeah so a buy n hold strategy beats yours. I could have bought SPY 3 months ago and 5x’d your return.

replies.author: Downtown_Extension_6
replies.body:
You're right that buy-and-hold SPY crushed this over the last 3 months in absolute terms, no argument there. But we're measuring two different things, and that's the whole point.  
  
This isn't a strategy with an investment period, so "opportunity cost of not being in the market" doesn't apply, there's no capital sitting on the sidelines. It's a **log of independent buy recommendations**: each row is a user running the agent on a given date and getting a signal. Apr 23 doesn't mean "I chose to buy then" , it means someone got that call then. The list exists to measure one thing: **were the signals right, relative to the market at the moment each was made?**  
  
So the correct benchmark isn't the index over a fixed 3-month window — it's the index over each signal's *own* window, then aggregated. Done that way: **+6.2pp average alpha vs SPY, 65% beat rate** across 66 signals.

Happy to drop the full per-signal table with both benchmarks if you want to check it.
